reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not address Cu segregation, liquid-like surface layers, or premelting in FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles. E1 describes a generic MD melting simulation procedure, and E2 discusses thermal analysis of a different HEA (CoCrFeMo0.85Ni) for phase stability, providing no support for the key premises.
premises: Copper has a lower cohesive energy than other elements in FeNiCrCoCu, driving surface segregation upon heating
Surface segregation of Cu forms a liquid-like layer that locally lowers the melting point
This liquid-like layer propagates inward to govern premelting onset
Suppressing Cu segregation (e.g., by passivation) will raise the premelting onset temperature
The mechanism is dominant in 5–10 nm nanoparticles
